record.paper_title: Progress in Nuclear Astrophysics: a multi-disciplinary field with still many open questions
record.original_question: What is the correct 22Ne+α reaction-rate input, especially for the 22Ne(α,n)25Mg channel, in rotating massive stars, and how does that rate change the efficiency of the s process and the resulting production of p nuclides during later supernova explosions? The paper states that s-process production in massive stars remains sensitive to this rate, that recently questioned measurements can reduce the 22Ne(α,n)25Mg rate by a factor of 5 relative to an earlier reference value, and that the same uncertainty propagates into p-process yields.

evidence.quote: Despite this important progress, the s process in massive stars remains affected by the 22 Ne+α rates which have been recently questioned by sub-Coulomb α-transfer measurements [14, 15]. In particular, a reduction of the 22 Ne(α,n)25 Mg rate by a factor of 5 with respect to the previously determined rate of Ref. [16] reduces the efficiency of the s process. Shedding light on this rate remains a priority for nucleosynthesis studies.

The decrease of the 17 O(α,γ)21 Ne rate [12] by a factor of 10 with respect to the former rate of Best et al. [13] directly affects the synthesis of p-nuclei. A similar sensitivity is expected for the still questioned 22 Ne(α,n)25 Mg rate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider rotating massive stars (initial mass roughly 15–25 solar masses with rotation) in which helium burning and subsequent carbon shell burning activate the alpha-induced reactions on $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}$, namely $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(\alpha,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$ and $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(\alpha,\gamma)^{26}\mathrm{Mg}$. The former liberates neutrons that drive the slow neutron-capture (s) process, producing nuclei heavier than iron; its seeds are later partly photodisintegrated during the subsequent core-collapse supernova explosion to yield the proton-rich (p) nuclides.

Recent sub-Coulomb $\alpha$-transfer experiments suggest that the astrophysical reaction rate of $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(\alpha,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$ in the relevant Gamow window (corresponding to helium- and carbon-burning temperatures, roughly $T \sim 0.2$–$1$ GK) may be smaller by up to a factor of about 5 than the previously adopted reference value.

Problem: Determine the correct stellar reaction rate $N_A\langle\sigma v\rangle(T)$ of $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(\alpha,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$ (and of the competing $(\alpha,\gamma)$ channel) over the temperature range relevant to helium and carbon burning in rotating massive stars, and quantify how the resulting rate modifies (i) the efficiency of the weak s-process and the integrated production factors of s-only isotopes (e.g.\ $^{70}$Ge, $^{76}$Se, $^{80}$Kr, $^{86,87}$Sr) and (ii) the yields of the p-nuclides produced when the s-process seeds are processed by the subsequent supernova shock.
artifact.status_search_result: The 22Ne(α,n)25Mg rate remains under active investigation as of 2024–2025. A 2025 review (Eur. Phys. J. A) discusses the state of the art and persistent uncertainties; new direct measurements at Notre Dame (Shahina et al.) and the deep-underground LUNA/INFN-LNGS effort are ongoing, with first long low-energy beam time planned for winter/spring 2024/2025. The rate and its astrophysical impact on s- and p-process yields in massive stars are not definitively settled.

status_evidence.title: The 22Ne(α,n)25Mg reaction - state of the art, astrophysics, and perspectives
status_evidence.snippet: Review of state of the art and remaining uncertainties in the 22Ne(α,n)25Mg rate and its astrophysical perspectives.
status_evidence.claim: The rate remains an active subject of measurement and review in 2025.

status_evidence.title: The Ongoing Deep Underground Measurement of 22Ne(α,n)25Mg at INFN-LNGS
status_evidence.snippet: Background tests done in late 2024; first long low-energy beam time foreseen for winter/spring 2024/2025.
status_evidence.claim: Direct underground measurements are still in progress, indicating the rate is not yet definitively constrained.

status_evidence.title: Constraining the 22Ne(α,γ)26Mg and 22Ne(α,n)25Mg reaction rates using sub-Coulomb α-transfer reactions
status_evidence.snippet: Sub-Coulomb α-transfer measurements suggest a substantial reduction of the previously adopted rate.
status_evidence.claim: Recent indirect measurements have called the older reference rate into question, motivating ongoing work.
